subject: Ontariopay — post-demo DPA / SCC options and next steps
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: David Santos <dsantos@ontariopay.com>, Marcus Liu <marcus.liu@ontariopay.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya.rao@ontariopay.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 5 Jul 2027 14:12:00 -0400
Subject: Ontariopay — post-demo DPA / SCC options and next steps

Hi David / Marcus,

Great to talk earlier — thanks for the time and the product walkthrough. To recap the compliance items you flagged during the demo and to keep momentum:

- SOC 2 status: you mentioned your security team would want a recent SOC 2 summary and a statement on in-scope systems.
- GDPR / cross-border: Ontariopay needs clarity on whether we can accept data subject requests and how the DPA will be scoped (controller vs. processor).
- SCCs: you asked us to indicate which SCC module(s) Redwood would propose for your architecture.

Next steps I propose (short timeline):
1) You share your internal legal/security contact (if different from Priya) and any baseline questionnaire we should complete — ideally this afternoon.
2) Redwood to send a concise DPA intake (we use a short spreadsheet) + two SCC options: the standard processor module vs. a controller-processor split variant.
3) We attach a SOC 2 executive summary and a recommended DPA template for your legal team to review.

I attached a short DPA intake workbook to capture data flows and a checklist of SCC implications so we can quickly recommend the right module. Can you confirm Priya is the right reviewer for legal? Also, any target date for finalizing the DPA?

Thanks — will loop Ben and Marissa on legal/contract path once we hear back.

Best,

Soojin Lee
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0142

Attachments referenced: ONT-DPA-intake.xlsx (short intake to capture flows / retention), SCC-module-comparison.pdf (high-level option table)

From: David Santos <dsantos@ontariopay.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya.rao@ontariopay.com>, Marcus Liu <marcus.liu@ontariopay.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 6 Jul 2027 09:18:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Ontariopay — post-demo DPA / SCC options and next steps

Thanks, Soojin — good recap. Priya and I spoke after the call; a few clarifications from our side:

- SOC 2: we need the SOC 2 (Type II) executive summary and the control scope (what systems are covered). If you can share a short redacted summary that'd be perfect.
- DPA: we typically start with a DPA where Ontariopay is the Controller and vendor is Processor. However, there are two product paths at play on our side: some flows will involve Ontariopay-controlled tokens (we'd still expect Redwood to be Processor) and one upcoming feature might mean Ontariopay is co-controller for a subset.
- SCCs: our legal prefers the two-step approach — start with processor SCCs, and if co-controller flows look unavoidable, discuss a controller-processor module.

I've attached our internal compliance intake template (short) and a note on retention expectations. Priya will lead the DPA review; cc-ing her here. Can Redwood confirm whether the Processor SCC module covers:
  * subprocessing lists/approval flow
  * data export controls / EU-to-US mechanisms
  * standard breach notification windows (we need ≤72 hours)

Tentative timeline: we want a first-draft DPA and SCC recommendation by next Wednesday (13 Jul).

Thanks,

David Santos
Head of Platform
Ontariopay
dsantos@ontariopay.com

Attachments: ONT-SOC2-2026-summary.pdf (we will send ours once you confirm format)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 6 Jul 2027 11:04:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Ontariopay — post-demo DPA / SCC options and next steps

David / Priya — thanks for the fast reply and for confirming Priya as the legal lead. We can meet your timeline for a first-draft by next Wednesday. Quick answers below and what we'll deliver by EOD tomorrow:

Answers:
- SOC 2: attaching our SOC 2 executive summary (redacted) and a short note on the in-scope services (search, inference runtime, logging pipeline).
- Processor SCC coverage: yes — our recommended Processor SCC module includes subprocessors list & approval flow, EU→US transfer mechanism (SCCs + supplementary measures where needed), and a ≤72-hour incident notification SLA. We'll document the subprocessors and the escalation path in the DPA.
- Controller/Processor split: if Ontariopay identifies co-controller flows, we recommend the controller-processor module for that subset and will include language in the DPA template to support a hybrid approach.

Deliverables (tomorrow EOD):
1) Redwood-DPA-template.docx (tracked changes friendly)
2) SCC-module-comparison.pdf (processor vs. controller-processor tradeoffs)
3) Completed ONT-DPA-intake.xlsx (we'll populate the first tab with our assumptions; please review)

Action items for Ontariopay:
- Priya / Marcus: confirm the data flow owner for the tokenized feature by COB Wed so we can mark it as potential co-controller flow.
- David: confirm breach notification window requirement (you mentioned ≤72 hours — we will commit to that in the DPA).

If it's helpful, we can set a 30-min touch on Thursday to walk through the DPA template.

Best,

Soojin Lee
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai

Attachments: Redwood-DPA-template.docx, SCC-module-comparison.pdf, ONT-DPA-intake.xlsx

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 7 Jul 2027 09:03:00 -0400
Subject: Fwd: Ontariopay — post-demo DPA / SCC options and next steps

Ben / Marissa — forwarding the thread and the inbound asks from Ontariopay. Key points for legal/CS engagement:

- Timeline: first-draft DPA + SCC recommendation due 2027-07-13.
- SOC 2: David wants an exec summary + in-scope list (attached). I've included our SOC 2 redaction and a short scope note; validate that the scope phrasing is sufficient for their legal.
- SCCs: recommend we lead with the Processor SCC module; include controller-processor clauses as optional language.
- Incident SLA: commit to ≤72 hours for notification; confirm whether we need to bake in remediation timelines or just notification.

Ask: Marissa, can you take point on reviewing the Redwood-DPA-template.docx and suggest any non-negotiable language we should avoid? Ben, if you can pull the current subprocessors list and a short write-up on our EU→US safeguards, I will merge them into the intake workbook tonight.

I will prepare the first draft deliverables and send to Ontariopay EOD tomorrow. There may be a small request from them on subprocessor approval windows — we should decide internally whether we allow "reasonable objection" vs. explicit approval.

Thanks — Soojin

[Soojin's internal note: slot 30-min Thursday review with Priya if they accept — coordinate calendars]
